# `workspace/WorkspaceCompositor.js`

> **Source:** `plauna/workspace/WorkspaceCompositor.js`

WorkspaceCompositor.js — WebGPU blit pipeline for GPU panels. Architecture: - Each GPUPanel owns a GPUTexture render target - Compositor blits all visible GPU panels onto canvas swap chain each frame - DOM panels are rendered directly by browser (compositor only handles WebGPU) - Simple blit shader: just copies texture to canvas Pipeline components: - Sampler: Linear filtering for panel textures - Bind group layout: Single texture binding (binding 0) - Shader: Simple vertex + fragment shader for texture copy - Blend state: Alpha blending for layered panels Render loop: - Called by WorkspaceManager each frame - Iterates visible GPU panels in z-order - Creates bind group per panel - Issues draw call (6 vertices for quad)

## Classes

### `class WorkspaceCompositor`

WorkspaceCompositor - WebGPU texture compositor. Compositor pattern: - Blits GPU panel textures to canvas swap chain - Handles only WebGPU panels (DOM panels rendered by browser) - Simple texture copy pipeline (no post-processing) - Alpha blending for layered panel support

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor(options)` |  |
| `init` | `async init()` | Initialize the blit pipeline. Pipeline initialization: - Creates sampler with linear filtering - Creates bind group layout for texture binding - Creates shader module with vertex + fragment stages - Creates render pipeline with blend state Shader details: - Vertex: Full-screen quad (6 vertices) - Fragment: Texture load at (0,0) for full texture copy - Blend: Standard alpha blending for layered panels |
| `compose` | `compose(encoder, gpuPanels, canvasView)` | Compose all GPU panels onto the canvas. |
| `initPanels` | `initPanels(panels)` | Hand off GPU device to panels (they need it to allocate textures). |
| `destroy` | `destroy()` |  |

## Notes & Examples

### App & widget lifecycle

Plauna apps and widgets follow a **mount → update → unmount** lifecycle; services (storage, command bus, theming) are *injected* rather than imported, so the same widget runs in the editor, the OS shell, and standalone.

**See also:** [Plauna Architecture](/plauna/architecture.md) · [Plauna Overview](/plauna/overview.md)

### App & widget lifecycle

Plauna apps and widgets follow a **mount → update → unmount** lifecycle; services (storage, command bus, theming) are *injected* rather than imported, so the same widget runs in the editor, the OS shell, and standalone.

**Example: Widget with full lifecycle**
```js
import { Widget } from 'plauna/core/Widget.js';
import { useStorage, useCommands } from 'plauna/hooks.js';

class CounterWidget extends Widget {
  mount(container, services) {
    // Inject dependencies
    this.storage = useStorage(services);
    this.commands = useCommands(services);
    
    this.el = document.createElement('div');
    this.count = this.storage.get('count', 0);
    this.render();
    container.appendChild(this.el);
    
    // Register commands
    this.commands.register('counter:reset', () => {
      this.count = 0;
      this.render();
    });
  }
  
  update(props) {
    if (props.increment) this.count++;
    this.render();
  }
  
  render() {
    this.el.textContent = `Count: ${this.count}`;
    this.storage.set('count', this.count);
  }
  
  unmount() {
    this.commands.unregister('counter:reset');
    this.el.remove();
  }
}
```

**See also:** [Plauna Architecture](/plauna/architecture.md) · [Plauna Overview](/plauna/overview.md)
